title: The East Road
objective: Take the east road to Harrow.

default.text: You pack what you have. At the bar Aldous gives you bread for the road without being asked, and charges you three coins less than the posted rate. Nothing more is said.
You have been in Crestfall three days. You know more than you did, and not nearly enough, and the rest of it lies to the east.
All three of the powers in the town have asked you for something or offered you something.
You took the Compact's coin.
You carry the Covenant's stone.
You owe none of them anything, which has its advantages.
You have a direction, and somewhere to go, and a letter that may or may not be a warning. You have pieced together enough to see the outline of the thing, though you still cannot see what it is.
It is getting light, and the east road is waiting.

default: You leave before the market opens.
text.commander:
You have made your arrangements before you go: the Compact's message, if you took it, the Covenant's ward, if you are wearing it, and whatever you have built with the Rootless.

None of them has bought you. You are going east to find out the truth for yourself.
text.arcane:
Before you go you spend an hour at the Tallow's writing table going over three days of notes. You are better prepared than [missing person] was, you think. You know more, and you understand more of what you know.

You hope that will make a difference. You are quite aware that it may not.
text.ranger:
Before you go you check your pack, as thoroughly as you always do. Everything is there.

From the market square you look down the east road. It is empty at this hour, which may be good or may be suspicious, and you had better decide which before you are a mile along it.
text.cipher:
You say goodbye to nobody before you go. It is the cheapest kind of goodbye, and the safest. If you don't come back, nobody will remember that you chose to leave them.

It may be good sense, or it may be loneliness that has turned into a method. You stopped being able to tell the two apart some time ago.

choices.text: Go to the Compact gate and confirm the arrangements.

text: Cael is on the gate. He nods when he sees you, pleased that you are doing what you said you would. He gives you one thing more: a place to leave word, a password, and a way of sending news back if you find anything important.
"Be thorough, [sir/ma'am]," he says. "Whatever is in those ruins, Commander Vorne needs to know exactly what it is before he can act."
You don't much like the word act.

text.text: "You read our mail and still took the job," Cael says. "I respect that."

choices.text: Go and see Maret at the camp before you leave.

default.text:
She knows you are going. She has put a few things together for you: dried food from the camp stores, a bitter herb that Pol, the camp's healer, has prepared, and a map of the east road drawn by hand, with the places the camp has explored marked on it.

"Lira drew it," Maret says. "She remembers the outskirts better than the rest of us. Those marks are hers."

She asks for nothing in return. You both know you owe her for it all the same.

choices.text: Take the east road.

default.text: You leave Crestfall alone before dawn, heading east while the town is still making up its mind whether to wake.

default: The cobbles last for a mile. Then the road is packed earth, and then it is hardly a road at all, only the way people have happened to go.

After the second mile the forest begins to close in on either side. It happens gradually, as a room changes when the light goes. At first the trees stand back and you can see the sky. Then they come nearer and the sky is a strip above you. Then they meet overhead, and you can only take it on trust that the sky is there.

The silence here is wrong in a way you are beginning to understand. It is as if something has taken the place of sound. There are no birds and no insects. The wind moves the branches over your head, but without the noise that wind makes in branches.

default.text: You read this road at midnight, and so far it has held no surprises.

text.commander:
You walk the road as you would advance on any position, watching the ground and the angles and the places where something might be waiting. It is poor ground: trees close on both sides, no view to speak of, and only one way to go.

You keep moving. The only answer to poor ground is not to stop on it.
text.arcane:
The pressure you have felt since you came to Ashenveld is stronger out here. It grows a little with every half mile. You walk with your notebook open.

You write: the effect grows steadily as one gets nearer, and not by leaps. That fits a single source that does not move, rather than something spread about. The source is ahead, and it is in one place.
text.ranger:
You read the land as you walk. The curse shows in it plainly enough, if you know what to look for: the way the grass leans, the fungus along the roots, the patches where the soil is a shade darker than it should be.

The curse came from the east and travelled west. You can see which way it came in the ground itself.
text.cipher: You walk and keep an eye on your own attention: what it goes to, what it passes over, what seems more interesting than it ought to and what seems less. Even this far from the ruins the curse is in the air, and you want to be sure you notice it rather than let it steer you without your knowing.

choices.text: Keep going, and read the road as you walk.

default.text: You keep going. The road gets narrower, and the trees come closer. Two hours along, the road shows you something.

choices.text: Stop at the last milestone and look back at Crestfall.

default.text:
From here the town is a smudge of smoke above the trees. You can make out the shrine roof and nothing else. You stand there longer than you need to.

Then you turn back to the road.

default: The place Edric described is easy enough to find if you are looking for it. On the left the tree line turns sharply over a few yards and leaves a notch in the canopy. It may not be natural. Or it may be perfectly natural, and the Covenant has simply watched this spot long enough to make something of it.

default.text: Edric's stone is heavy in your pocket.
default.else: You are not carrying Edric's stone, but you stop anyway.

default: There is something about the place. The air is still, and still in a different way from the stillness round about. If the Covenant's scholars called this a nexus, they found something real.
text.commander: There is something here, and it is real. It is not exactly threatening, but it is concentrated. You stop a moment longer than you need to.
text.arcane:
The air here is thick with it. You stand in the notch and let your senses reach out, and you can feel several of the curse's channels meeting near the surface, like rivers coming together, except that you cannot see the rivers and what they carry is worse than water.

So the Covenant's scholars know their business. That is worth knowing.
text.ranger: What animals are left in this forest have been keeping away from the spot. You can see it in the tracks: paths that come towards it and then turn aside, again and again, worn into the ground by going round. Whatever is gathered here, the creatures have given it a wide berth for months.
text.cipher: The place is real, and the Covenant found something genuine here. So their scholars do understand how the curse works, and have mapped it, and it is not all doctrine. That makes them both more dangerous and more useful than you had thought.

choices.text: Place the Covenant marker stone here.

default.text:
You put the stone where Edric told you to, and stand back, and wait. Nothing happens that you can see or hear.

Either it is working on a scale you can't perceive, or it is doing nothing at all. Either way you have done what you said you would, and the Covenant owes you a small favour.

choices.text: Place the stone, and feel what it does when it touches the ground.

success.text:
You set the stone down where the tree line bends, and keep your hand on it.

It pulls, very slightly, as a lodestone pulls at a needle. It does not pull away from the forest but towards it. Whatever Edric's people made it for, it is not holding anything back. It is feeling out where the note is strongest, and marking the place.

You take your hand away. The stone stays where it is.

success_at_cost.text: You set the stone down and feel it settle into the ground, and something under the ground settle towards it. You can't tell what it is doing, except that it is not nothing.

failure.text: You set the stone down and feel cold stone and wet earth, and nothing more. Whatever it does, it doesn't do it for you.

choices.text: Kneel, and feel where the stone wants to go.

default.text:
You kneel with the stone in both hands and lower it towards the ground until you feel the pull. It wants to go a little to the left of where Edric said, nearer the bend, and you let it.

The moment it touches the earth, the note under the road leans towards it. The Covenant is not slowing anything with these stones. It is mapping it.

choices.text: Remember the place, and keep moving.

text: You fix the place in your memory and move on. The spot is real, and Edric's scholars know what they are about. The Covenant is more dangerous than it looks.

default.text:
Where the road dips down to a stream there is a lean-to of planks and canvas, with a mule tied to a post in front of it. A woman in a Compact coat sits on an upturned crate, eating bread with one hand. There is a crossbow across her knees.

She stands up when she sees you. She doesn't raise the crossbow, but her hands are not quite steady.

"Sera," she says. "Quartermaster. The lieutenant said someone might come along with a packet, [sir/ma'am]." She looks past you up the road, and then into the trees. "Nobody else has. Not for a while."
default.else: Sera is still by the mule, not looking at you.

choices.text: Hand over the packet.

default.text:
She takes the packet, puts it inside her coat without looking at it, and counts twenty coins into your hand.

"A patrol went east nine days ago," she says as you turn to go. "Six of them. They were meant to be back on the fourth day." She looks at the mule. "I keep the feed ready."

choices.text: Lift the seal and read the packet first.

success.text:
You turn your back on her as if to check your pack, and work the seal up with your thumbnail. It comes away cleanly.

There is one sheet inside: an order to make ready billets in Crestfall for thirty men and a commander, signed in Vorne's name and dated a month ago. So Cael knew. He has known all along.

You press the seal back down, and it holds.

success_at_cost.text:
The seal comes up, though not cleanly. You read the order: billets in Crestfall for thirty men, Vorne's name at the foot, a month old. Cael knew.

When you press the seal back down, one corner won't lie flat.

failure.text:
The seal tears. It is a very small sound, and she hears it anyway.

Sera looks at the packet in your hands and then at your face. "I'll have to report that," she says. She doesn't sound angry, only tired. She doesn't pay you, and she doesn't take the packet.

choices.text: Nod to her and keep walking.

default.text: You nod to her and walk on, with the packet still in your pack. She watches you all the way to the bend.

text.default:
You hear it before you see it, or rather you hear that the sound is wrong. Something is moving through the undergrowth with the rhythm slightly off, as though it had learned to walk in a forest by watching something else do it.

It comes out of the trees on your left. It is a deer.

But it is wrong. Its legs move in the proper order, but the back legs come half a beat behind the front, so that the whole animal looks like a machine. Its eyes are open but they follow nothing. It holds its head at an angle that serves no purpose; it is not scenting the air or watching anything, only holding it there.

It crosses the road thirty yards ahead of you and goes into the trees on the other side without stopping.
text.commander:
You watch it cross. Your skin is crawling, and you couldn't say why.

So the curse has got into the animals too, which means it has spread a good deal further than the ruins. You fix the place in your mind: how far you are from Crestfall, and in which direction.
text.arcane:
The residue on the deer is thick. It has been under the curse for months, perhaps longer. The curse goes differently in animals. People keep enough of themselves to suffer the difference between what they were and what they are becoming. Animals seem to lose even that.

In any sense that matters, the deer is no longer there.
text.ranger:
You have tracked deer in a dozen forests, and you have never seen one move like that.

What is wrong with it is quite particular. It is a hunted animal that has stopped being afraid. Fear goes so deep in a deer that you could not take it out without taking out the deer, and whatever the curse does, it goes all the way down to the bottom.

You wait a couple of minutes after it has gone, listening for anything that might have been following it.
text.cipher:
So the curse takes animals as well as people, and in much the same way, it seems. It leaves the body going about its business, and takes away whatever was paying attention.

You fix the place in your head and go on.

choices.text: Follow it into the trees and see what it is doing.

bonus.label: Branch walked the first mile with you
You read this road last night

success.text:
You track it fifty yards through the undergrowth and find it standing in a small clearing, doing nothing at all. It isn't eating or drinking or resting. It stands with its head at that wrong angle, breathing quite normally.

For ten yards or so round about, the ground is different. The grass is lower and the soil darker. You crouch at the edge of it and look. The curse is concentrated here, and there are tracks from a great many visits. The deer has come back to this place over and over again.

It chose to come here. Whatever the curse does to wanting, it does not do away with it. It turns it to something else.

success_at_cost.text: You follow it far enough to make sure that it is doing nothing but stand in the trees. You come back to the road feeling that you have seen something you couldn't describe if you tried.

failure.text: You follow it and lose it almost at once. It moves in a way you can't predict. You go back to the road, and after even that short while in the trees the road is a relief.

choices.text: Get close enough to touch it.

bonus.label: You read this road last night

success.text:
You leave the road slowly and come at it from downwind, a step at a time, stopping when it stops. It doesn't notice you. Close to, its eyes are not quite still. They drift, and settle, and drift again, and every time they settle they are pointing east.

You touch its flank. It is warm, and it doesn't flinch.

When you step back it walks on through the trees, eastward, at the same wrong pace.

success_at_cost.text: You are within arm's length when a stick snaps under your boot. Its head comes round slowly and it looks straight through you. Then it walks on. You stay crouched in the bracken until your legs cramp.

failure.text: You are almost there when it bolts. It goes straight through the place where you are standing, as though you were not there at all, and its shoulder knocks you off your feet. By the time you are up again it has gone.

choices.text: Read its trail backwards instead.

default.text:
You leave the deer to its walking and go back the way it came. The trail is easy to follow. It comes the same way every day, with the same wrong stride, to the same place: a clearing a hundred yards in, where the grass is shorter and the soil darker in a ring ten paces across.

It does not wander. It comes here, and stands, and goes away again. There is still one thing it wants.

choices.text: Let it go, and carry on along the road.

default.text: You let it go. Whatever it is now, it is nothing to do with what you came for. You carry on east.

text.default:
Somebody is coming towards you down the road, moving fast, not quite running. It is a middle-aged man carrying a good deal more than anyone ought to carry at that pace. He would rather be far away than comfortable.

He sees you and doesn't slow down. If anything he goes a little faster.

You step to the side of the road so that he can pass if he wants to. He very nearly does. Then, a couple of yards past you, he stops.
text.commander:
He turns round with the face of a man who has made up his mind to something and is already sorry.

"You're going the wrong way," he says.
text.arcane:
He stops and turns, and looks at you as if weighing how much you might want to know against how much he wants to tell.

"You're going east," he says. He doesn't make it a question.
text.ranger:
He stops and turns. His pack was made for the army, by the straps and the frame of it, though he is not in the army any more. His boots are worn down on the outsides of the heels, which tells you something about him you can't yet place.

"Going to Harrow?" he says.
text.cipher:
He stops and turns, and you take his measure quickly. He is running from something. He is not afraid of you in particular. He is afraid of what is behind him, and you happen to be heading towards it.

"Turn round," he says. He doesn't bother with good morning.

choices.text: "What did you see? Tell me."

success.text:
He tells you. He was trying to get across Ashenveld to the coast, and the east road was the quickest way. Last night he camped a mile beyond Harrow, and some time in the night he woke up in the middle of the road, sitting upright, facing east.

He hadn't walked there. He doesn't walk in his sleep. He has no memory of moving at all.

"I was facing east," he says. "Like something wanted me to look."

He gives you something without being asked: a small figure carved out of bone, which he picked up in Harrow. "Don't know why I took it," he says. "Don't want it."

success_at_cost.text: "Harrow's empty," he says. "Don't go into Harrow." He looks up the road behind you. "Go back to Crestfall, if you've any sense." He has walked on before you can ask him anything else.

failure.text: He shakes his head and keeps going. In a few seconds he is past you, and in half a minute he is a speck in the distance. He doesn't look back.

choices.text: Stand aside and let him pass.

default.text: He goes by without looking back, and the sound of his feet going west soon dies away. You carry on east.

default: Half a mile further on, the road shows you something.

It is a camping place, and an old one. More than a year's leaves have settled in the fire ring, and still nobody has kicked the stones apart. One person camped here, once, and it was not the man you have just passed. There is a ring of stones for the fire and a patch of cleared ground, all neatly done by somebody who knew how to camp and always tidied up before leaving.

default.text: You know the way it is laid out. You have seen it before. The ring of stones is three flat and one tilted. It was a mark, and a habit, and you noticed it years ago when you watched the person who taught it you do it for the first time.
default.else: You know the way it is laid out. You have seen it before. The ring of stones is three flat and one tilted, a mark the two of you always used.

default: [missing person] was here fourteen months ago, travelling east.
text.commander: You go over the camp methodically. They stayed one night. They left heading east, by the way the place faces. And they were in good order when they were here: the camp is tidy and the fire properly built. Whoever made it was not in any trouble.
text.arcane:
The residue here is clear enough to read. One person, one night, and the curse had not gone deep in them when they left. They were themselves, and wide awake.

You feel something that is very likely relief, and is fear as well.
text.ranger:
The camp is easy work for a tracker. One person stayed one night. The fire stones are set in a way you have never seen anybody else use, and the cleared patch is exactly the size of a bedroll.

They went east, and the tracks, faint on this ground, bear it out. Fourteen months ago, travelling east.
text.cipher: You know that way of setting the fire stones. It is no coincidence: the tilt of the one stone, the spacing, the choice of this clearing. Somebody was here, and they wanted you, if you came, to know it was them.

choices.text: Go over the camp carefully. They may have left something.

success.text:
Under the edge of one of the fire stones, put there on purpose and weighted down, there is a torn piece of cloth. They left it.

On the cloth, in ink that has partly run, there are three words. You read them several times to be sure you are reading them right.

[player]. Go home.

They knew you would come. They knew it well enough to leave you this at the first place you would stop. And they did not want you to.

success_at_cost.text: At the edge of the camp you find a scuff in the soil, a footprint going east. It tells you which way they went, and nothing more. There is nothing here left for you.

failure.text: The camp gives you nothing more than you have already. You have the stones, and that is enough. You go on.

choices.text: Follow the trail. They're ahead of you.

default.text: You leave the camp without touching anything and go on east, faster than before. The trail is fourteen months cold, but it is still a trail.

text.default:
This is Harrow.

There are twelve houses, a well, a shrine and a barn the village shared. Everything stands where it was built and where it ought to be.

Nothing is moving.

The silence here is not like the silence of the road. It is heavier, the silence of a place that used to have people in it and has none now. Harrow is not a ruin. The houses are whole. A door stands open in one of them, but not because anybody broke it; somebody simply went out and did not think to shut it.

You walk into the main street, and your footsteps are the only sound.

Through the windows you can see meals laid out on three tables. They were set and never eaten. Nobody was interrupted. They laid the tables, and then they went.
text.commander:
You go through Harrow as you would clear any village, house by house, quickly, looking for danger and for anything worth knowing.

There is no danger. There are no bodies and no blood, and no sign that anybody panicked.

Everything says these people left quite calmly. The food on the tables is months old. They went as though they meant to be out for the day and back for supper.
text.arcane:
Harrow is soaked in the curse. It is the kind of thickness that builds up over months of steady exposure in a closed place.

You read the history of it. The curse built up here slowly, and then at some point it reached a level beyond which everyone in Harrow stopped wanting to stay. Short of that, nothing changed at all.

You understand now how it happens. The curse does not make anybody do anything. It only changes what they would rather do. And in the end everybody here would rather have gone into the forest, and all at about the same time.
text.ranger:
Harrow looks like ground something has passed over.

The doors were left open calmly, not in a panic. Food was cooked and never eaten. There is a child's toy beside a doorstep, put down there on purpose, you would say, and not dropped.

All the tracks out of Harrow go east. They were made over days and weeks, each person going when their time came, but every one of them went the same way.
text.cipher:
Harrow can be read like a letter, so you read it.

Nobody fought, and nobody ran. They simply went, calmly and one at a time, as people leave a place they no longer care to be in, until there was nobody left.

What you want to know is not what happened here. It is what made staying seem worse than going east.

choices.text: Look round Harrow. Whatever is here matters.

default.text: You take your time in Harrow. The afternoon light is going, and you would like to be under a roof before dark.

choices.text: Go through quickly, and reach the edge of the forest before dark.

default.text:
You go briskly through Harrow and out the other side. From the eastern wall of the village you can see where the forest begins in earnest, a dark line perhaps a mile off, or less.

You sleep in Harrow's barn. It is better to have walls round you tonight.
